executiveSummary: GM1982's 2025 identity, centre, population, 101 neighbourhoods, 34 BAG places, 98 settlement labels, three stations and twelve road/ferry border links are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Land van Cuijk extends along the rain-fed, regulated Maas and includes distinct primary-defence reaches, outside-dike land, the Raam system and many dispersed cores. The official regional worst-case is EDO 36: water above assessment level or dike failure, not a municipality-wide scalar. The generic river preset instead holds exactly 1.505207 m, 45,318 affected people-equivalent and identical service values from T+24 through T+72 without a boundary hydrograph, dike section/failure, outside-dike footprint, arrival or recession. Current public Waterinfo has four fresh local Maas-level observations and forecasts classed normal only through T+24; it supplies no GM1982 T+48/T+72 forecast and no inundation or defence state. Generic pluvial forcing ignores the Raam, high-Maas backwater/closure interactions, terrain, groundwater, sewers, controls and current projects. Seven unrelated nonzero individual hazards share the exact same first five neighbourhoods. The graph includes A73/A77/N-road links and the audited Bergen–Vierlingsbeek ferry, but does not encode that the N324 road bridge is integral with Stuw Grave, that the ferry ceases at very high Maas levels, or operational rail/bridge/route and care access. Public registers identify 445 water assets, Enexis/Brabant Water/Ziggo territories, one grid-planning sample, 216 antenna sites, 67 education records and Maasziekenhuis Pantein, but not live topology, state, backup or restoration. Exact consequences and first-72-hour recovery must be suppressed until governed event, lifeline and action evidence exists; missing or horizon-limited data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1982 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshot retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1982 as Land van Cuijk and reports 92,817 residents, density 272/km², 24.5% aged 65 or older and 13,260 one-person households; the generated centre [5.8519167258135045, 51.666990974159106] is inside the 2025 boundary.

One hundred and one neighbourhood rows in 33 districts sum to 92,845 residents, 28 above the municipality total (+0.030%); households sum to 40,740 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 22,760. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 92,817 without rewriting the source rows.

BAG supplies 34 active places, all contained by the generalized municipality, while BRT supplies 98 settlement labels: 33 woonkernen, 14 deelkernen, seven gehuchten and 44 buurtschappen. BAG/PDOK place data are Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT are edition-based CC BY 4.0.

District heat and public charging cover 0/101 neighbourhoods; home value and tenure omit 12, cars per household 18, and several benefit fields nine. Publisher null, suppression and non-applicability remain NoData, not zero; annual residents do not measure visitors, rail/road/ferry users, patients, workers or event-time occupants.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Maas system, Stuw Grave controls and public Waterinfo observations/forecasts
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS asset pages inspected 3 September 2026; Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts 3 September 2026 04:29Z
supports: The Maas is a rain-fed regulated river. Rijkswaterstaat monitors levels continuously and progressively opens/strikes the seven stuwen before high water; Stuw Grave is normally struck around approximately 1,500 m³/s, after which it no longer regulates the high-water level. A typical threshold is static context, not a live command or event boundary.

The Grave complex combines a traffic bridge, two stuw openings with 60 schuiven, two lock chambers (one closed since 1975), local operation, a fish passage and about three metres of level difference. Sambeek is another upstream control. Asset function does not establish present state, passability, failure or emergency capacity.

The deployed CC0 Waterinfo snapshot contains four fresh GM1982-assigned water-level observations at Gennep, Grave boven, Sambeek beneden and Sambeek boven, observed 2 September 2026 17:30Z and publisher-classed normal. These point observations are not an inundation surface, dike state or all-clear elsewhere.

The rolling Waterinfo forecast exposes the same four local level points at T+1, +6, +12 and +24, all classed normal, but no local T+48 or T+72 value. The endpoint has no single published model-cycle issue time; response time, request window and per-value validity are retained. Missing later horizons are NoData, not zero hazard or persistence.

Waterinfo is public CC0 unless component-specific exceptions apply and the public service is explicitly not mission-critical. Observations/forecasts remain non-causal until a governed adapter binds station, datum, issue/valid time and event boundary conditions.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Cuijk–Ravenstein and Boxmeer–Cuijk primary defences, Raam system and current works
evidenceSources.edition: Current project page inspected 3 September 2026; plan-outworking and preparation status through June 2026
supports: The Cuijk–Ravenstein project covers the Brabant Maas side between the Katwijk/Mook rail bridge and A50 at Ravenstein. The preferred alternative was completed in 2022; the project is currently in plan-outworking, with an adopted draft project decision and contractor selected in late 2025. Planning or construction need is not an acute failure.

The water board's 2022–2027 programme treats Cuijk–Ravenstein (21 km) and Boxmeer–Cuijk (17 km) as distinct improvement reaches. Current board reporting funds completion of planning and preparation for realisation; almost 80 of 110 km of its Maas dike is being improved across the wider area.

The Lage Raam, Hooge Raam, Halsche Beek and Rode Beek projects seek more controllable storage and discharge under drought and heavy rain. Raam-valley storage can be relevant when extreme Raam discharge and high Maas occur together. Project intent and future works are not present control state or capacity.

The June 2026 board record says Ruimte voor de Maas at Oeffelt and Lob van Gennep are intended to lower high-water levels but were at the end of plan-outworking with insufficient realisation budget. It also identifies remote-process control of stuwen, pumps and schuiven and planned renewal of the central system; this is governance/dependency context, not live telemetry.

No standard blanket machine-reuse licence was identified on the project pages. A usable flood input still needs the authoritative geometry/model package, CRS, unit, version, licence, dike/control assumptions, valid time, uncertainty and NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Climate adaptation, water nuisance and dispersed-area context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal climate-adaptation and water-nuisance pages inspected 3 September 2026; policy horizon to 2050
supports: The municipality distinguishes heavier rain, drought, heat, storm and more frequent Maas overflow, and promotes rain retention, greening and climate-resilient public space with Aa en Maas. Hard-surfaced business areas such as De Beijerd and Het Riet are specifically described as contributing to runoff and heat.

The municipality says its water-nuisance policy is ambitious but drought and heat policy require more ambition. Proposed measures and self-help guidance are programme/context records, not completed defences, live drainage capacity, a warning or a quantified T+72 forecast.

Its water-nuisance page distinguishes high groundwater, private-property/sewer problems and dangerous flooded roads/cycleways, provides an out-of-hours escalation path and links users to Waterinfo. These different mechanisms and responsibilities must not be collapsed into one flood scalar.

No machine-readable municipality-wide stress surface, sewer topology, live pump/control state or blanket standard reuse licence was identified on the pages. Missing local response state remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024–2027 and regional care-risk profile
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile version 8 June 2023, adopted for 2024–2027; regional care-risk profile 2024
supports: VRBN's measure-case water scenario is high Maas water/EDO 36: water above assessment level or failure of dike rings 36/36A leading to significant low-lying outside- and inside-dike flooding. The document explicitly warns that local scenario probability and impact differ from regional scale.

The profile says the existing rings met the then-current legal norm but higher standards and improvement programmes extend toward 2050. It identifies striking Maas stuwen as a vulnerable human-operated process and seeks further impact analysis for electricity, gas and telecom. Meeting one norm is not an all-clear; programme need is not current failure.

Regional exercise scenarios include an exceptional 200 ha forest/heath fire under extreme dryness, wind and difficult access, while saying urban cores are not directly threatened at regional scale. It also frames power/gas outage as 8 hours–6 days, drinking-water and wastewater disruption as health-relevant after 24 hours, and telecom/ICT loss as 48 hours.

The regional care profile identifies Maas high water, navigation incidents, nature areas, rail and hazardous-material sites as relevant and calls for coordinated care-chain preparation. These are official scenarios and governance context, not local activation, staffing, capacity, supplies, completed actions or forecasts. No standard blanket reuse licence was found.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Noord-Brabant / ProRail / OVapi / Gemeente Bergen / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Road, Maas crossing, ferry, rail/transit and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB generates twelve border links: two A73 ends on one physical corridor, A77, N272, two ends of N324, three N277 boundaries, N264 to Gennep, plus the audited Bergen–Vierlingsbeek ferry. Scenario capacities 260/150/55 are generalized ceilings and same-corridor ends are not additive throughput.

The N324 Maas crossing is the traffic bridge integrated with the Grave stuw/sluis complex, so hydraulic/control, navigation and road states share a physical site. Static route geometry does not encode common-cause failure, road/bridge inspection, emergency restrictions or alternate crossing state.

Gemeente Bergen's official high-water guidance says the Bergen–Vierlingsbeek ferry goes out of service at very high Maas level. The graph correctly retains its audited geometry and context-only current status; a threshold-conditioned closure still needs an event-valid authority state and must not be inferred from a scalar depth.

ProRail supplies Cuijk, Boxmeer and Vierlingsbeek stations and the Nijmegen–Venlo/Maaslijn geometry, including the Maas rail crossing near Katwijk/Mook; GTFS supplies 184 stop areas. Geometry and timetables do not prove trains/buses/ferries running, vehicles, passenger/evacuation capacity, accessibility or restoration.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 assigns Maasziekenhuis Pantein in Beugen to GM1982: 24/7 SEH and acute obstetrics, seven treatment rooms and 12,886 visits reported for 2025. The CC0 questionnaire is dated context, not live acceptance, occupancy, staff, generator endurance, incident capacity or route passability.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / NDW / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water, provider, grid-planning, antenna, education and current-context registers
evidenceSources.edition: Public-context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; provider and contributor dates vary
supports: Full non-generalized-boundary containment assigns 445 HWH records: 38 sewer pumps, 16 surface-water pumps, 15 sluices, 375 weirs and RWZI Land van Cuijk. Managers are Aa en Maas for 405, generic Waterschap for 38, Limburg for one and null for one; only 50 capacities are non-null and 395 null. Every status is 'gerealiseerd', which is register context, not live operation. HWH is CC BY-SA 4.0 and contributor completeness varies.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting point lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas (updated 7 September 2025), Brabant Water (29 December 2025), Ziggo media (7 September 2025), and no drainage polygon. Reference-point responsibility is not municipal completeness, topology, outage, pressure/quality, capacity or restoration.

The one NBNL HPS Haps sample reports withdrawal 92 MW existing, 87 required and 54.6 MW/112 requests queued; injection 83.7 MW existing, 115.5 required and 96.2 MW/81 requests queued; TenneT classes 3/3 and 11 projects, earliest 2028. This is quarterly/monthly large-user planning context with no exact licence identifier found, not live load, reserve, outage or project completion.

RDI supplies 216 antenna-installation sites and DUO supplies 67 education records: 43 primary, nine secondary, four special and 11 other. RDI's WFS states no standard reuse licence/cadence; daily DUO RIO is CC-BY with version unspecified. Neither proves coverage, backhaul, power, shelter role, occupancy, staffing or supplies.

The bounded deployment assigns no local NDW road situation, KNMI weather observation/warning or seismic origin, or RIVM PM2.5 point. Empty source/time/spatial matches are NoData, not open roads, normal weather/air, zero seismic hazard or an all-clear.

corrections.validation: Warnings, dike/stuw/pump decisions, inspection, evacuation/reception, crossing control, Maasziekenhuis continuity/transfer, temporary water/sanitation, utility repair, fuel/food/medicine and welfare actions show authority, issue/valid time, resource and completion state; only confirmed actions alter recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Enexis/Brabant Water/gas/telecom/wastewater topology, current control state, backup endurance, priority users, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Maas outcomes require upstream discharge/hydrograph, travel time, stuw and defence state, outside-dike geometry, breach/overtopping, arrival and recession; public normal station classes through T+24 are not an inundation forecast and local T+48/T+72 forecast coverage is absent.

Raam and urban/rural water outcomes require rainfall, terrain/soil/groundwater, receiving Maas level, sewers/catchments and current weir/sluice/pump controls; plans and 445 register points do not supply that operational model.

Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS omit event-time road/bridge/ferry/rail/bus operation, inspection, accessibility, ambulance/freight/evacuation capacity and restoration; an empty NDW match never proves access.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM omit visitors, commuters, recreation/camping occupancy, livestock, assisted-evacuation needs, live hospital demand, shelters and household stocks across 34 dispersed places.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, weather, roads, crossings, care and utility states can change after audit completion; stale, empty, horizon-limited or out-of-coverage inputs must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Reconcile EDO 36, rings 36/36A, Cuijk–Ravenstein, Boxmeer–Cuijk, high-ground tie-ins, outside-dike land, Stuw Grave/Sambeek and upstream Lob van Gennep/Oeffelt assumptions across Noord-Brabant and Limburg.
Integrate Waterinfo observation/forecast points as time-scoped non-causal context; require a governed hydraulic adapter and preserve no local T+48/T+72 forecast as NoData.
Join Raam-valley/high-Maas, pluvial, groundwater, sewer and managed-control scenarios without mixing project intent, current observation, official forecast, EDO scenario or synthetic model output.
Audit N324/Grave common-cause bridge-stuw-sluis state, Katwijk/Mook rail crossing, high-water ferry suspension, A73/A77 and alternate care/supply routes without summing shared corridors.
Test common neighbourhood ranking across Maas/Raam water, paved-area heat, Overloon/forest-heath fire, wind/winter and named cyber targets.
Use Maasziekenhuis's registered acute role as dated context only and define validity-aligned acceptance, diversion, backup and access contracts for the first 72 hours.
